sections.h2: Where do you record and find property records in Travis County?
sections.html:
The Travis County Clerk's Recording Division files and keeps real property records for the county, including deeds and tax liens. Its main office is at 5501 Airport Blvd., Ste. 100B, Austin, TX 78751, open 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with the mailing address P.O. Box 149325, Austin, TX 78714.

The clerk also lists two sub-stations open 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM: the Civil Family Courthouse at 1700 Guadalupe St., 4th Floor, Ste. 4.300, Austin 78701, and the Raul Martinez Office Building at 4011 McKinney Falls Pkwy #1200, Austin 78744. The main recording phone line is (512) 854-9188. Effective April 1, 2026, the Guadalupe Street location offers Official Public Record recording, DBA filings and marriage licenses with no appointment, but not plat recording.

sections.h2: What is Travis County like for sellers?
sections.html:
Travis County is a large, fast-growing county that includes Austin. The Census Bureau counts 1,389,670 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 7.7 percent from the April 2020 estimates base, on 994.05 square miles of land.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020-2024: $523,000.
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 52.1 percent.
  • Median gross rent: $1,744.
  • Building permits in 2025: 15,059.
  • Median household income: $99,611 (2024 dollars).

With that mix, deed work in Travis County includes many investor sales, estate transfers and rental properties, and a clean recorded chain of title is what keeps a closing on schedule.

sections.h2: How do you record a deed with the Travis County Clerk?
sections.html:
Bring or mail the original signed document, because the clerk will not record a copy. Real property documents can be filed in person or by mail, and the clerk says recording is completed as soon as the document is received.

Most documents other than plats are scanned, given an instrument number and returned the same day by mail or immediate return for walk-in customers. Subdivision plats are not returned the same day. Payment can be by cash, credit card, check or money order payable to Travis County Clerk, and card payments add a fee: $3 on transactions under $100 or 3 percent on $100 or more.

A deed must also meet the state's execution rule: acknowledged before a notary or other officer, or sworn before two subscribing witnesses, under Property Code Section 12.001(b).

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Travis County?
sections.html:
An Official Public Records document costs $25.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, part of a page or rider. The last page needs at least three inches of space at the bottom or the extra page fee applies.

Discharges and DD214 filings and child support liens and releases carry no charge.

sections.h2: How can you search Travis County property records online?
sections.html:
The clerk offers a public records search, and the clerk's page links to the search site at tccsearch.org. Indexes for most recorded documents are online, and redacted images for recordings run from the mid 1980s to present.

Redacted images are copies with personal identifiers such as Social Security numbers blocked. Court case data updates every 24 hours, and newly filed document images take about 72 hours to appear online. For documents older than the online range, the clerk says its permanent library holds millions of documents dating to the 1800s, with older ones on microfilm.

  • Documents printed from online at home: free, marked as unofficial copy.
  • Clerk-made or emailed copies: $1.00 per page.
  • Certified copies: $5.00 per document plus $1.00 per page.
  • Self-serve photocopies: 20 cents per page; microfilm or computer printouts: 25 cents.

sections.h2: What does a name search cost?
sections.html:
A basic electronic search for one name or business is free, plus the cost of copies. Searching microfilm or paper data costs $10.00 per name for each ten-year period searched.

The fee schedule also lists grantor and grantee searches at $10.00 per name for up to ten years, plus federal and state tax searches at $10.00 each and UCC-11 searches at $15.00 per debtor. For a deeper search, the clerk says its office will provide an estimate.

sections.h2: Who can file electronically in Travis County?
sections.html:
eRecording is limited to specific filers under Local Government Code Section 195.003, including licensed Texas attorneys, banks and credit unions, title insurance companies and agents, federally approved lenders, licensed regulated lenders and state agencies.

The clerk lists several approved submitter companies and invites anyone interested in becoming a submitter to contact the office. A homeowner selling alone does not qualify directly, so most sellers go through a title company, which typically e-files the deed on closing day.

sections.h2: What else should a Travis County seller know about the record?
sections.html:
Expect the record to show more than the deed: liens, trustee sale notices and tax liens are filed with the same clerk. Notice of a trustee sale of real estate is posted for a $2.00 fee, and state and federal tax liens have their own filing charges.

Property tax is a separate system: the appraisal district sets value and local taxing units bill, while the clerk only records documents. For closing figures, ask the Travis County tax office for the current bill. Before listing, search the owner's name for open liens and make sure the deed in your chain matches the name on the contract.

faqs.q: Where is the Travis County Clerk recording office?
faqs.a: The main office is at 5501 Airport Blvd., Ste. 100B, Austin, TX 78751. Sub-stations at 1700 Guadalupe St. and 4011 McKinney Falls Pkwy also take recordings on 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM hours.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Travis County?
faqs.a: The fee is $25.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus $0.25 for each indexed name beyond five. Missing the grantee's mailing address adds $20.00 or twice the recording fee.

faqs.q: Will the clerk record a photocopy of my deed?
faqs.a: No. The clerk requires the original document with original signatures and will not record a copy. Plan for a notarized original when you file.

faqs.q: Can I search Travis County property records for free?
faqs.a: Yes for online indexes and images. Printing from your own computer is free, with an unofficial copy watermark. Searches of microfilm or paper records cost $10.00 per name per ten years.

faqs.q: How long do new documents take to show online?
faqs.a: Newly filed document images take about 72 hours to appear online, according to the clerk. Recording itself is completed when the clerk receives the document.
